processing: A cultivar, not a finished tea; little is documented about what it is usually made into. Teas from the Mengshan area are typically processed as green tea.
harvest_season: An early-budding cultivar; Sichuan green tea is typically picked from early spring.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it; no description is recorded.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Sichuan green tea: a clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Typical of Sichuan green tea: soft green leaf.
taste_profile: No tasting description is recorded; expect the fresh, vegetal cup typical of Sichuan greens if made as a green tea.

brewing.notes: A general method for green tea; a tea from this cultivar should be brewed for its style.

vintage_note: Rarely if ever sold under the cultivar name. Nothing specific is recorded; as with other Sichuan greens, tea from it would normally be sold as the current spring's harvest.
description:
Mengshan 23 is a clonal tea cultivar selected from the Mengshan tea population at Mingshan near Ya'an in Sichuan. It is a shrub with medium-sized leaves and an early start to the season, diploid. It is a plant name more than a shop name.

Tasting notes here are otherwise what is typical of Sichuan green tea, not a record of this plant.

If a seller names it, ask what style was made from it and which garden it came from.
history: Selected from the Mengshan tea population by single-plant selection between 1976 and 1988, by the Mengshan Tea Farm in Mingshan County, Sichuan Agricultural University and the farm administration bureau of the Sichuan provincial agriculture department.
